text: The best part of BG3 is you can roleplay
anything. Cat? Been done. Wizard? Too
milktoast. But a campaign where a cube
is the star? That's the type of crazy
this world needs. Can you beat Baldur's
Gate 3 using a companion cube?
Introducing Kubert, my custom-built
portal-inspired companion cube. Created
at my request by Scurby to bring my
dreams to reality. For this challenge,
I'll be attempting to beat BG3 using
only the improvised melee weapon action
in combination with this proxy box ally
to indiscriminately Domvey Run. But
that's not all. A second action will be
available this time as I have access to
portal technology. An unlimited use
appropriately colored themed version of
the arcane gate spell. Outside of these
two moves, no action or bonus actions
are allowed. That's the rules and at the
end there will be cake. Though the
indestructible cube is our leader in
spirit, it is still an inanimate object.
For that reason, we have Wheatley, our
cube's primary handler. In case you
weren't aware, cubes lack the legs
required to walk. Improvised melee
weapon, however, does allow you to carry
your target with you by default. And
when combined with kidnapping, you can
carry your six-sided buddy through the
ship towards the game's first combat
encounter. It's the cube's turn to carry
us now. Never before have proxy box
tactics looked this cute. To close the
gap on a ranged opponent, I employed
fancy pants portal technology. As our
leader, Kubert chose to free
Shadowheart. Then together, we enter the
helm of the ship. Shadowheart apparently
lacks the strength necessary to lift an
80-lb block over her head. And turns
out, touching a flaming cube is a sure
fire way to get burned. To avoid the
embarrassment of game overing in the
tutorial level, there was no choice but
to rush our companion through portals to
reach the transponder. It did the job.
Tanked the dragon like a boss. Fell from
the nautiloid to safety. And we begin
act one on the beach as always. For
once, bypassing the initial intellect
devourers is a no-brainer. Kubert
created calamari and one week man joined
our ranks. BG3 has a party limit of
four. A rule we will follow. Three
people, one cube. Despite clearly
looking stronger than I, neither of
these individuals can lift 80 lbs. So
victory over goblins rests entirely on
the backs of Zevlor and the humans.
Planned to just portal up to the high
ground to heroically AFK it. Though
Zevlor seized the moment to pull a will.
Noticing his competency, all efforts
then switched to helping Zevlor traverse
the battlefield. Allowing him to
dumpster these clowns before instantly
appearing on the high ground and
shattering all immersion. In the grove,
we fed Kubert some gruel. Took a power
nap. Impressed the locals. Probably. And
carried on down the road into the goblin
camp. The mere act of crossing this
bridge magically frees Withers. Meaning
Will can become the most daring D&D
class of all time. The human fighter.
Now that we have a party who can utilize
our friend, it's time for trial by
combat. Being a shared tool, we must
always remain grouped around the cube to
keep pumping attacks. It deals 2D4 base
damage. Which seems good until you
realize it's garbage because for no
reason the devs decided improvised
melee's damage should never scale with
strength like normal weapons do. Likely
an oversight. Much like the lesser known
quirk that it has no vertical range
limit. Further exploitation of that
mechanic will be explored. When you're
melee only, ranged targets suck. Wow,
real insightful script there, past
proxy. The biggest annoyance is you'll
end up eating many opportunity attacks
like an idiot while sharing a weapon you
constantly body block each other trying
to grab. As for non-combat struggles,
lockpicks are banned. But anything's a
lockpick if you waste enough time. Over
at Waukeen's Rest, Florrick showcased
her usual canonical stupidity. Failing
to understand a portal is a fire escape
exit. Then our cube's apparent thirst
for blood led to the deaths of local
hyena and gnoll kind. It's here I
observe the gnolls are the first
creature stupid enough to attack a fully
damage immune ally. Nor will they be the
last. This run taught me some enemies
appear to be scripted to always hit the
closest possible target, no matter how
little sense it makes. Woodland
creatures with their bludgeon resist are
more pain than they are worth. As is any
other enemy who is even somewhat
competent. Leaving only the goblins.
Pretty sure we got scanned in the
chicken chase contest. No one makes our
dear leader look bad and lives to tell
the tale. Can't explain how I pulled off
this further than usual ranged
improvised weapon attack. But there's no
denying it looked badass. As I gave it
to Crusher, the realization of the new
disaster that this challenge run
actually is began to sink in. Portal
tech is OP in many ways. But making
portals cost 1/3 of our team's total
actions. And frustratingly, I learned
enemies will shove the cube into a pit
when they see the chance. Re-summoning
it is another costly action. Over the
course of 22 minutes, I kited these cube
haters all over the place. Managing to
secure just two kills in that time
before needing to flee to avoid a game
over. Then when Shadowheart got
arrested, it was a blessing in disguise.
As after escaping she can unlock the
secret burrow side door for some easier
goblin encounters. 4v1 are the type of
odds we need. While normally I'm the one
using doors to cheese, a goblin reversed
Uno'd me. As when standing in a doorway,
one is incapable of being targeted by
cube. It's been difficult, but thanks to
the many brain-dead easy outnumber your
enemy encounters, eventually level four
is achieved. Unlocking a massive power
spike. The Tavern Brawler feat. Let's
read what it does. When using an
improvised melee weapon, your strength
modifier is added to the damage and
attack rolls. I know it was subtle, but
I emphasized damage because in classic
Larian fashion, the tooltip is a lie.
Tavern Brawler does not add any damage
to improvised melee weapons. Nor does
strength. Thinking maybe it was my
modded cube, I tried other household
items. But no, it's just bugged. And
probably no one ever noticed. Because
does anyone actually use this? In a top
three [ __ ] of all time scenario, a
toppled statue did not hurt the goblin
directly in its path. Yet somehow dealt
with the will who was clearly outside of
danger. Partially my fault for not
thinking more with portals. As with
clever placement, you can pull off some
sick gorilla tactics to crush your
enemy's guts. One goblin appeared so
intimidated by our team, it chose to
jump into the spider pit rather than
face death by furniture. Inspired by its
decision-making, Minthara too was led
there. Triggering a 29-round
slobberknocker where the heart always
wins. Arcane gate really shouldn't be
locked behind a six-level spell slot for
how fun it is. Halsin carried his own
jailbreak. Then our cube. A bond was
formed between them. And together we
played Draugr Ragzlin like a fiddle. Bro
walked right into position for our cube
to drag him down to hell like Kirby in
Smash Bros. In many ways, the goblin
camp felt like a much needed tutorial in
how to portal combat. Tieflings
celebrate their heart-marked hero. The
cult of the cube is forming. With their
lives temporarily saved, it's off to the
Underdark to attempt solving our damage
problems. Biberbangs have Balin
cornered. And using the only power we've
got, he's been rescued from his plight.
Returning to his wife rewards the gloves
of uninhibited Kashigo. This item adds a
1D 4 bonus to improvised melee weapons.
[music] To test it out, I cubed Will in
his face. Oddly, it did the damage
twice. Being confused, science got done.
Turns out, the Ring of Flinging is the
culprit. This item doesn't say it buffs
improvised melee weapon. Yet it secretly
does while at the same time lying to you
about it in the combat log. As I did not
expect that, it was the main factor in
deciding never again will I trust these
developers' lies. I'll do my own
science, thank you. As our damage will
forever be terrible, combat is largely
reliant on boxing one guy to death,
escaping through a portal, and coming
back for more. A single frog turned out
to be our kryptonite as apparently this
melee action is considered a reflected
projectile. Mostly out of desperation,
the druids were next on the chopping
block. Things got weird with a pig. And
we entered the mountain pass still level
four to challenge the kobolds. An enemy
much closer to the power of our party.
Still took three separate attempts of
fleeing, but eventually we ended these
kobolds to reach level five. The biggest
jump in power we will ever see. As now
we can attack twice per turn. This new
tool allowed us to be victorious in
combat without having to flee in the
first time in hours. But just barely.
The initial crush guard refused entry to
our suspicious group. So Will ran a
distraction. Turns out once one person
is in combat for trespassing, everyone
else is allowed to walk on by freely.
Did some shopping for a crit fish stat
stick. Then turned on the residents
using the tried and true zerg, die,
retreat like a wuss technique. Volo,
being a secret millionaire, kindly
bought up all of our worthless crap to
fund Withers' ever-growing medical
bills. The gith acted much more casual
than one would expect after seeing the
murderer return who fled after killing
their friends. But considering we're led
by a hexahedron, who are we to judge
their culture? Countless deaths occurred
whilst clearing out the crèche. And I
gave up before the boss knowing my own
limits. Back in the Underdark, I let one
enemy at a time enter this portal up to
the cliff. Handling Geck and his bros
before leaving zombies to rot on a
cliff. Breaking down doors is a time
sink. As is destroying these now defunct
turrets. But 40 XP is 40 XP. It was this
action which made me question
everything. 19 hours played for just
level five is a new PR. Not a good one.
It's time to go to the Aperture Science
Labs to find out if anything can improve
improvised melee weapons. The
spell-based classes I wrote off right
away. Paladins' smites are a no. Sneak
attack? Also no. Monk's staff two
doesn't appear to work. But then I got
to ranger. Swarmkeeper ranger to be
specific. These subclass reactions are
the only ones I could find of any class
in the game which trigger when
improvising. Adding a massive 1D6 per
turn without giving up most of the
fighter benefits. There's just one
problem. It is annoying. For some reason
the game pops up three reactions every
single time like a virus-ridden Windows
XP computer. And you have to click the
right one or it's wasted. Turning an
already difficult playstyle into the
most frustrating BG3 experience one
could ask for. But I am desperate for
damage like a Valve fan is to the number
three. This build is an abomination, but
it's staying. Level ones are no longer a
threat. Will is having a valid crash out
in response to our new pop-up playstyle.
And it would be Auntie Ethel who is the
first boss our party is capable of
defeating. Shortly thereafter, the
owlbear mate helped us ding level six.
Unlocking the War Domain cleric's three
extra attacks per long rest. Which
automatically work with improvised
melee. Was hoping it would be enough to
carry us through the boat encounter and
reach Grymforge. However, that is a pipe
dream. They demolished barrel walls
strats, too. That is an impossible
puzzle. Leaving the mountain pass undead
as the better option. Headed them to a
legend portal and used them for 35 turns
because skellies can't jump and bludgeon
resist is a stupid no fun overused
mechanic. Walmart Gandalf was not at all
impressed by our cube's aesthetics.
Leaving him behind we carry our
companion into the Shadow-Cursed Lands.
Immediately began Act 2 by bashing in
this goblin's brain. Totally metagame
the drider caravan future allies in our
usual way. Took a break to poop. Then
let our leader handle the negotiations
at Last Light Inn. What's in the house
is that thing? Jaheira is no doubt
confused, but more about for the cube
recognizing her people's savior. And
afterwards the Harpers are followed to
the ambush site to face a lone drider.
Fully expected this to be a pain in the
ass like every other moment of this
existence so far. However, for perhaps
the first time in recorded history, the
Harpers carried my weak team. Tossing
out dozens of magical missiles to secure
the W. Hubert freed the pixie. Its
blessing got us to Moonrise. And while
shopping there I found two more items
that buffed the hit chance of our
attack. Unsurprisingly both tooltips are
different and neither one mentions
improvised melee weapons at all. Why is
it that every tooltip related to this
action is wrong? Going to do things
slightly different today and head
backwards to Grimforge using the
elevator. While killing duergar is
always a blast, the real reason I came
here is a scientific expedition. We can
mine. We can craft. But can you use
portals to lure Grim outside the arena?
Sadly no. The robot refuses to take
them. And neither will the lava
elemental. But by using improvised melee
weapon we can trigger the swarmkeeper's
likely steroid driven bee reaction to
knock it down to Grim where they are
perfect little pals who refuse to fight
one another. The lava surfaces it
occasionally drops can superheat Grim,
which is a neat observation. And should
you wait long enough, I'm talking 26
minutes of spamming the spacebar ending
your turn in a row long, sometimes the
elemental will accidentally cleave Grim
while wailing on my invulnerable cube.
Got game over due to some [ __ ] But
in the second round of my time wasting,
Grim lost enough HP to spawn in the
imps. During the chaos Grim repeatedly
slammed his elemental body by mistake
proving elementals do have feelings.
Grim broke its little lava heart. They
turned on each other the same way an NPC
does to a player when we're acting like
a dick. Because the elemental heals
while standing in lava, it pulled off
some next level cheese. Tearing poor
Grim into pieces. As the crucible was
still covered by the elemental's lava, I
checked to see if you can craft using
it. And interestingly enough you can.
What a strange and unusual experience
all that was. We leave this test subject
in its new found habitat. Returning to
the Shadow-Cursed Lands. Daddy himself
helped me reach the 7. An event I'll
make sure never happens again. This time
we multiclass into Great Old One
Warlocks. Or GOO as the kids like to
call it. Their class passive makes crits
frighten nearby enemies. And also on
non-crits sometimes in an interaction
unique to improvised melee weapon. This
spreads the debuff yet doesn't explain
how in the combat log. Took Surgeon
Malice up the lift to his little waiting
room where strangely he stops fighting.
Which is probably the only reason this
was a winnable encounter as his bludgeon
resistance makes him take two to three
damage at most. Defending an allied
portal ain't skill in this story. So
thankfully when there's a barrel there's
a way. Probably should say a hundred
barrels. Stacked so much crap in front
of this portal that nobody is going to
touch it. I'd say this was a triumph but
it was a tad too easy. To further help
Halsin I played hide and seek in the
cemetery with a million little shadow
[ __ ] A bit excessive how many there
are when your DPS is this bad. On the
bright side they all violently explode
twice once 39 have been slain. With
Halsin's Shadow-Cursed adventure stuff
complete, we advanced to the Gauntlet of
Shar. Adding portals to these puzzles
really got me excited. Both boring maze
trials are a huge success. What threw me
for a loop however was the nightmare
that is the selfsame trial. Even whilst
cheating to make the clones naked. Much
like the other 90% of Act 2, they are
bludgeon resistant. But worse than that
is the cheater's folly debuff. A
mechanic I usually ignore. It reduces
your strength when you hit a non-clone.
So much so that whoever is affected will
no longer be able to wield the cube.
That's not an option. Instead each copy
must be soloed by themselves. Brutal
versus clones not following my stupid
rules. Running around the room and using
the door helped. And eventually Will was
able to clutch it with 7 HP. Because two
damage is absolutely massive to us, I
used my theoretical degree in crate
engineering to reach the top of this
door near Balthazar's bedroom. As
mentioned earlier, this portal is a
recolored copy of the existing arcane
gate spell. And if you didn't know, cuz
why would you, that spell cannot target
items. But if you place a corpse on top
of a box, then you can target the corpse
to create illegal portal locations. Just
walk on through to glitch over locked
doors. I'll be impressed if someone else
uses that somehow. But there's my plus
two damage ring acquired. A chest wall
near the invulnerable door was
constructed for the Umbral Tremor
engagement. Though that idea fell apart
once the undead justiciar started
clipping through the door. 57 minutes of
pure pain went by as this boss is immune
to all damage taken except the jellyfish
thing of our swarmkeeper reaction. Back
up the stairs to find Balthazar
afterwards only to realize I hadn't even
aggroed half the enemies in the room.
Took the sudden combat as an opportunity
to betray Balthazar saving us all a lot
of trouble with the earlier failed chest
wall being a crucial instrument in
Flushes demise. Act 2's main objectives
are roughly half over. So the grind
begins. This is a bold that was going to
be my eighth level thing. However, turns
out he's immune to bludgeoning. Choosing
something more my power level, we nearly
bested these one HP crows. To satisfy my
cube's taste for blood and my lust for
XP, the bad guys were slaughtered. You
don't know how good your life is until
you spend 97 rounds trying to kill two
stupid eyeballs with a heart-shaped
block praying to crit for one damage.
After the bad guys, naturally comes the
good guys. Don't let the Harpers fool
you. They'll pretend they're the
Shadow-Cursed. But should a cube connect
with one cranium, it will happily chase
you through portals into it with
absolutely no regard for their own
well-being. Well here I remembered
Dammon could craft the flawed Helldusk
set for me. So luckily he wasn't dead
yet. But don't worry. He was moments
later. Fully confident this item
wouldn't work as it doesn't mention
anything on the tooltip. The gloves
damage roll does not. But the bleed
effect does? An absolutely massive
discovery. Cuz now I can have one
character become a Wolverine barbarian.
When damaging a bleeding target, they
have a passive which also names them.
Plus the Act 1 boots of Stormy Clamour
can make my enemies prone. These two
conditions when stacked at once will
cause an enemy to skip their full turn
in an OP stun lock combo. Maybe this
idea ain't so bad. After what felt like
an eternity, a Shadow-Cursed hound got
us to level nine. The cloaker joined the
list of impossible targets for us to
kill. Though it did impress me when it
opened the door without having hands.
Fully expected Yurgir to be unbeatable
too. But the meme stun lock barb combo
kept him from doing anything for nine
rounds in a row making him the easiest
boss of Act 2. Went back to grind some
additional XP I'd missed. Then gathered
up the Morninglord Radiance buff, which
doesn't actually do anything. The Dream
Visitor's Blessing, the Blood of
Lefander, the Shar's Blessing, and
Isabel's too. Before heading on down to
place our gems and enter the Shadowfell.
Blue and orange got us to our
destination where it's time for the cube
to make a decision. Will it spare the
Nightsong?
I mean of course it will. The help
action's banned. What do you expect? And
now after what felt like months of prep
work, Ketheric stands alone awaiting us
on his tower top. I did have high hopes.
But Ketheric is pretty much the end of
any normal gameplay. There is no
realistic world where you are going to
beat this man using improvised melee
cube. The only plan I could come up with
was kiting him off this rooftop all
around the now extinct Shadow-Cursed
Lands dealing pitiful damage and
probably dying for hours on end.
However, portals off of his rooftop are
so far away that you exit combat if
taken. Meaning he won't follow. To
prevent combat from dropping a close
proximity box tower was constructed. I
led the way for Ketheric to follow
through and things are looking grand.
What likely none of you watching knew is
doing this instantly ends the encounter
and you win. I was beyond confused.
Checking the replay the man didn't lose
any HP. Nor did anything particularly
noteworthy happen. So what the hell is
this? I messaged resident BG3 detective
SlimX to find out. And he already knew
the answer. Replying with this developer
note. Handle freak edge case of him
falling off roof. A failsafe put in by
Larian to automatically end the
encounter should Ketheric somehow leave
his rooftop. Meaning this is not a bug
but an intended mechanic. Thank you to
SlimX for the open shut case. I
recommend you all check out his channel
if you enjoy well explained Baldur's
Gate 3 mechanics. Now continuing into
the colony past the flesh door, we have
a problem. Ketheric is still Ketheric.
We may have accidentally bullshitted our
way out of phase one. But now he's down
here still full health in an even more
restrictive arena. When two thirds of
your team is dealing zero to the guy and
the only one hitting for more than zero
is doing like four, a straight up
victory will never work. It's time to
initiate proxy box tactics. Going to be
honest, I had no plan here. Just
construct a tower, see what happens.
Discovered that once you get too high up
portals will no longer reach the ground
so any strategy using that is gone. But
the dead body to start the portal on
items technique is a great tool to port
between boxes. My hope was that possibly
if I'm standing directly over top of
Ketheric a cube would crush him like he
can do with shoes. Though no luck was
being had in my trials. Portal looping
between boxes brings the cube back up to
my tower top allowing for repeated
attempts. Suddenly, and I don't know
why, Shadowheart teleported into combat
below. Opening up the ability for us to
now see Ketheric from up here. That
mistake helped as Kubert can now
gracefully land upon his head like an
unarmed nuclear bomb. I knew improvised
melee's unlimited vertical range could
be exploited somehow. With the portal
return loop, it's an infinite combo. And
unlike throw, shove, jump, or any other
gravity based attack, there is no damage
boost while being at a higher elevation
when using improvised melee weapon. The
damage is still trash. Most people would
be upset. I'm not even angry. This is
the nonsense I knew I signed up for.
Phase one went swell taking just only
about 58 minutes. Bro began his
transformation into Myrkul. Will tank
the frightened reaction. And I extended
our OSHA violation a few meters further
to have a bit of an easier time
targeting him now that he inched ever so
slightly over. Each cube connection puts
up one stack of the strength drain
debuff, so we can see Merkul took more
than 100, 114 to be exact, from
construction to death. This single
encounter took a little over 3 hours,
but my glorious cube destroyed the
avatar. The netherstone's ours, and
that's what counts. No boxes are left
behind in this playthrough, as you'll
never know when you might need these
again. The bridge gith helped us reach
level 10 out the act, and it was off to
the sleepy gith intermission. Our
fearless leader led our team into the
astral prism, where nothing particularly
noteworthy happened. It was about time
nobody had bludgeoning resistance or
other stupid immunities. All the hard
work into handcrafting this build is
paying off. We begin act three with the
not so challenging goal of entering the
city. Purchased horns of the berserker
for its plus two damage. Attended the
coronation of Gortash as per Qbert's
demands, and then jump right into the
murder mystery quest line. It was
Wheatley in the kitchen with a cube who
killed the cook. Did a quick murder
spree in the devil's fee, where our
friend was turned to gold. Didn't
Rimworld already do this? That was
mainly done so we could infiltrate the
hells and take a bath, followed by
Indianan Jonesing the amulet of greater
health. Without any suspicion, our
escape is made. Dolor the invisible was
slain after being revealed by a barrel,
and Qubert alone would hover like it so
loves to do in cutscenes before the
murder tribunal. Opting to slay the
elephant will sacrifice and become the
first six-sided unholy assassin. Blood
ascension was not designed for such
stupidity. Main reason that decision was
made is for this ghost vendor and one
insane item, the crater flesh gloves.
These gloves on a critical hit will add
damage riders, unlike 99% of items on
honor mode. And in the bathhouse test
chamber, I discovered it works with the
ring of lingam to double that damage
entirely on hit. It's too bad there's no
way to get a second copy of such an
item, wink wink. On that note, let's
give all our best in slot gear to
Halsin, who's been chilling at camp
doing nothing, and then head on down
through the sewers. Right as you reach
this area, you can play with the
artifact or cast silence to dodge the
conversation with Halsin, aka Orin in
disguise. That simple dialogue skip
process has just duplicated every item
Halsin is wearing. The only caveat is
Orin has it all and still needs to be
killed in her temple. Thank you,
Dududek223, for sharing your console
viable gear dupe exploit with me and the
world. As we enter Manslaughter Chasm, I
figured I'd try to portal around the
sides to avoid the ghost, and this is
when I learned I'm an idiot. For the
last 10 or so videos, I've always said
this is a time trial where you need to
kill the ghost quickly to win or you
die. That is completely wrong, and turns
out if you outrange it once by standing
behind these little red foggy areas,
there are no consequences, and the fight
becomes a complete joke, giving you
unlimited time to clear these easy ass
murderers for solid XP. I love that I
still learn new things in this game, but
also I'm disappointed. I thought this
was the internet. Back in my day, when a
guy was wrong on the internet, 10
experts showed up to call him an idiot,
then correct him. Where are the experts?
Are any of you even real? Now that my
ranting's over and the far slayer of
ball is dead, we can make our way into
Orin's murder temple. I knew Orin would
be tough, and with the honor mode boon
of ball insta-killing a party member
every turn, it's likely impossible using
normal tactics. Nothing I can do can hit
these sanctuary channelers. The ceilings
are all too low to build towers like I
did against Cathrick. She cannot take
fall damage because of her unstoppable
condition, so knocking her out of a
makeshift tower or into a chasm will
never pan out. I spent about 30 minutes
death running her back with the help of
Withers all the way to the grease boys,
and 20 versus one, she soloed them all.
I was stuck on Orin for a couple days
and nothing I was trying was working.
Eventually reloaded and accidentally did
this. Sometimes when you stand by the
waypoint and click beyond the ball
temple door, you're able to clip through
it. This is actually an old bug that
Larian had tried to patch, but
apparently it still works if the door
has never been loaded in before. After
glitching through the door, Orin is
still transformed into Halsin, and you
can just toggle on non-lethal damage to
down her without any combat, triggering
the legit Orin death cutscene, granting
you her netherstone. But even better
than that is on the unconscious body of
Halsoaren, you will find that full set
of your equipment that the real Halsin
is wearing. Knock him out, too, to loot
your original set of gear. By the way,
this will work with any companion that
Orin can kidnap. It's not exclusive to
Halsin. Well, all of that solves one
netherstone problem. Using this method
means Orin didn't die for real. His
alliance with Gortash is thrown out the
window, and essentially I've traded one
boss for another. Though because Gortash
doesn't have an unfair one-shot kill
mechanic, it's a very favorable
trade-off for The other handy bit of all
this is out here there is a lot more
space for potential construction
